Class 1 · Chapter 6 of 8

Read clocks and calendars

Read the hands, then talk about days and months.

  1. See it
  2. Try it
  3. Practise it
  4. Print it
  5. Check it

This chapter works best after Measure length and weight. You can still look around, or jump to the check.

By the end I can…

  • I can read a clock.
  • I can find a later time.
  • I can find a day or month.

1 See it

Screen 1 of 4

Two hands, two jobs

The short hand is the hour hand.

The long hand is the minute hand.

Look at the short hand first.

Screen 2 of 4

O'clock

When the long hand points to 12, it is an o'clock time.

The short hand points to 3. So it is 3 o'clock.

Screen 3 of 4

Half past

When the long hand points to 6, half an hour has passed.

The short hand is between 7 and 8. We say half past 7.

Screen 4 of 4

Days and months

A week has 7 days. A year has 12 months.

After Saturday comes Sunday, and a new week starts.

Words to know
hour hand
The short hand. It tells the hour.
minute hand
The long hand. It tells the minutes.
o'clock
The minute hand points straight up at 12.

For parents

What your child learns

A clock has a short hand for hours and a long hand for minutes. Half past 11 is 11:30. 60 minutes make 1 hour. To add minutes, count on from the time shown.

A common slip

Children often swap the two hands. The short hand shows hours and the long one shows minutes. Check by saying the hour first, then the minutes.

5-minute home activity: Clock play

  1. Use a real clock or draw one with paper hands.
  2. Set it to 11:30 and read it aloud.
  3. Move the long hand 20 minutes on from 5:35.
  4. Count how far the minute hand moved in one hour.
